change.title: pr-93824-flat
change.description: Span Buffer Multiprocess Enhancement with Health Monitoring
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: A hung flusher process is never killed, so its replacement runs alongside it on the same shards
findings.body:
Processes are made with `self.mp_context.Process`, where `mp_context = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")` (lines 53, 105). That gives a `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`. In CPython, `SpawnProcess` subclasses `BaseProcess` directly, not `multiprocessing.Process`, so `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is always False and `process.kill()` never runs.

The old code called `self.process.kill()` with no condition. Now, in the `hang` case (line 236), the stuck process stays alive. `_create_process_for_shards` then starts a second process for the same shards (line 259), and both call `flush_segments`/`done_flush_segments` on the same Redis queues. That can produce the same segments twice. The stuck process is also leaked, and this repeats on every restart, up to `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS`.

The same check in `join` (line 346) means `terminate()` never runs either. Fix: check `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)`, or `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)`.

findings.title: join() stops looping once the deadline passes and skips the remaining processes
findings.body: When the deadline has passed, `break` leaves the loop. `terminate()` (line 347) never runs for that process or any process after it. The old code always terminated after the wait. Those processes are only stopped by the `stopped` flag, so a process that is stuck in Redis or Kafka keeps running past `join`. Use `continue`, or skip only the wait and still terminate each process (once the isinstance check at line 346 is fixed too).

findings.title: `spans.buffer.max-flush-segments` now applies per process, not per consumer
findings.body: `flush_segments` caps each shard at `ceil(max_flush_segments / len(self.assigned_shards))` (src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:382-384). Each per-process buffer now holds only its own shards, so each process can flush up to `max_flush_segments` per cycle. The whole consumer can flush `num_processes × max_flush_segments`. If the option is meant as a consumer-wide limit, divide it by `num_processes`, or document the new meaning.

findings.title: Cluster memory is queried once per process buffer on every submit
findings.body: `get_memory_info` returns `iter_cluster_memory_usage(self.client)` for the whole Redis cluster (src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:375-376), whatever the buffer's shards. Calling it for every buffer repeats the same INFO queries N times. `used` and `available` are each multiplied by N, so the ratio does not change. One call is enough, for example `next(iter(self.buffers.values())).get_memory_info()`.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag key: `shards` here, `shard` elsewhere
findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged `shards`. The `produce` timer (line 185) and `segment_size_bytes` (line 195) use `shard`, so dashboards can't group these metrics by one key. Also, `shard_tag` is a comma-joined list, so the number of distinct tag values grows with the shard combinations.

findings.title: Dead code: `_create_process_for_shard` and `if not process`
findings.body: Nothing calls `_create_process_for_shard`. `if not process: continue` (line 222) never fires, because Thread and Process objects are always truthy. Remove both.

findings.title: Docstring says one process per shard, but the CLI default is 1 process
findings.body: The CLI defaults `--flusher-processes` to 1 (src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py:434). Shards are spread round-robin over `min(max_processes, len(shards))` processes (lines 60-66). Only when `max_processes` is None do you get one process per shard.

findings.title: `time.sleep(0.1)` does nothing because the test patched `time.sleep`
findings.body: Line 15 sets `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None`. Since the test calls it as `time.sleep`, the patched version runs, so line 62 doesn't wait. The comment "Give flusher threads time to process" is false. Whether the flush happens before `join` sets `stopped` still depends on thread timing. To make this deterministic, poll until `messages` is non-empty, with a real deadline, e.g. a saved reference to the original sleep.

contracts.action: Restarting an unhealthy flusher process (kill, then respawn)
contracts.equivalent_path: The old _ensure_process_alive called self.process.kill() with no condition before _create_process
contracts.before_after: Before: always kill, then respawn. After: kill only when isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process), which is False for SpawnProcess, so the respawn runs next to the old process.
contracts.visible_effect: Two processes flush the same shards; segments may be produced twice to buffered-segments
contracts.failure_mode: A hung process leaks and keeps running until the consumer exits

contracts.action: join waits for all flusher processes before a deadline
contracts.equivalent_path: The old join waited for a single process, then terminated it
contracts.before_after: next_step.join(timeout) uses the deadline first. Each process is then polled every 0.1s until the shared deadline. Once the deadline passes, the loop breaks without terminating the remaining processes. With timeout=None there is no bound, as before.
contracts.visible_effect: Shutdown can leave flusher processes running
contracts.failure_mode: A stuck process is never terminated (and the isinstance check means SpawnProcess is never terminated at all)

contracts.action: Per-process SpansBuffer for flush, memory and queue-size checks
contracts.equivalent_path: A single SpansBuffer with all assigned shards
contracts.before_after: The flush cap is divided by each buffer's own shard count, so the total cap is multiplied by num_processes. Memory info covers the whole cluster and is fetched once per buffer.
contracts.visible_effect: More segments flushed per cycle; repeated Redis INFO calls

summary: The PR splits the span flusher into several processes, each owning a subset of the shards. Two lifecycle bugs: `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is False for spawn-context processes, so a hung flusher is never killed and its replacement runs on the same shards next to it. Separately, `join()` stops looping once the deadline passes and never terminates the remaining processes. Smaller points: the meaning of max-flush-segments changes, memory info is fetched once per buffer, metric tag keys are inconsistent, there is dead code, and the docstring and a test comment are wrong.
